note: Claims scoped to the RP2350: the core regulator (0.1.0) and the interface blocks, decoupling and supplies (0.2.0). Page numbers are the datasheet's (sha256 a638d678…) and the design guide's (release 3) printed pages. `requirement` gives a value range a tool can check, and `checks` the part of it a board's part values can show (SI units, package part names; `ccomp check package` reads them); `*_reference` values are measured on Raspberry Pi's minimal boards with `ccomp measure` (reference/*/measured.json) and are what the vendor achieved, not limits. `enforced_by` says which tool does.

claims.statement: The core regulator inductor is a fully shielded, polarity-marked 3.3 uH +/-20 % part with DCR <= 250 mOhm and Isat >= 1.5 A.
enforced_by: ccomp check package (inductance; DCR, Isat and shielding are not in a value string)

claims.statement: The inductor is placed the right way round: its marked pad (1) on the 1V1 output, pad 2 on VREG_LX.
enforced_by: generator (pads keep their nets; the footprint fixes the polarity)

claims.statement: COUT is 4.7 uF +/-20 % with ESR <= 250 mOhm and ESL <= 6 nH, and VREG_FB is taken from COUT.
enforced_by: generator (the feedback run ends at COUT's output pad)

claims.statement: CIN is >= 4.7 uF with ESR <= 50 mOhm, at VREG_VIN, with its own ground path to the QFN.
The switching loop area is kept as small as possible.
VREG_FB is fed from the output of COUT, avoiding routing directly underneath LX.
On a board with inner layers, the copper on the layer under the VREG_LX node is cut away.
enforced_by: generator keepout on the layer below

claims.statement: On the top layer, extra copper underneath the inductor is cut away and copper near the VREG_LX trace is cut back.
VREG_AVDD must be RC filtered: 33 Ohm and 4.7 uF.
VREG_PGND joins the main ground at one point.
enforced_by: generator (ground vias beside CIN's ground pad only)

claims.statement: The regulator layout should be placed first on any board design, and its guidelines must be strictly followed.
enforced_by: composer (milestone 5: critical blocks are placed and locked before the rest)

claims.statement: Each IOVDD, QSPI_IOVDD, USB_OTP_VDD and ADC_AVDD pin has its own 100 nF capacitor close to the pin.

evidence.note: Both minimal boards share one capacitor between USB_OTP_VDD and QSPI_IOVDD (QFN-60 pins 53/54, QFN-80 68/69), which the design guide states and defends as a space trade-off, and one between ADC_AVDD and the IOVDD beside it (44/45, 59/60), which neither document mentions.

claims.statement: USB_OTP_VDD and QSPI_IOVDD may share one 100 nF capacitor when space beside the regulator is short, at some cost in supply noise and top speed.
With the on-chip regulator, the two DVDD pins nearest the regulator get 100 nF each and the furthest gets 4.7 uF, each close to its pin.

evidence.note: Reference boards: QFN-60 pins 6, 39 get 100 nF (C8, C11) and pin 23 4.7 uF (C10); QFN-80 pins 10, 51 get 100 nF and pin 32 4.7 uF.

claims.statement: Decoupling capacitors sit close to their power pins; the reference boards reach each within 2.2-4.9 mm of copper.
A 4.7 uF capacitor connects VREG_VIN to ground close to the VREG_VIN pin.

The crystal is an Abracon ABM8-272-T3 (12 MHz, +/-30 ppm, ESR <= 50 ohm, CL 10 pF) with 15 pF load capacitors and a 1 kohm series resistor on XOUT, tuned for IOVDD = 3.3 V; any other crystal or IOVDD needs re-tuning and testing over temperature.
The crystal circuit's traces are as short as possible: their parasitic capacitance (budgeted at 3 pF with the pins) adds to the load.
enforced_by: intent max_length on XIN, XOUT (compiled to routing.json)

claims.statement: USB_DP and USB_DM each have a 27 ohm series resistor placed close to the chip.
enforced_by: intent max_length on the chip-side USB nets

claims.statement: R7 and R8 (27 ohm) are placed close to the chip, to meet the USB impedance specification.

citation.locator: §5.1 p.15; schematic note 'Make sure R7 and R8 are close to RP2350'

claims.statement: USB_DP/USB_DM run as a 90 ohm differential pair (on the 1 mm 2-layer reference: 0.8 mm tracks, 0.15 mm gap) over solid, uninterrupted ground for their whole length.

evidence.note: Connector side (R to J1) has ground under every millimetre on both boards. Chip side (pin to R) does not: unreferenced {"rp2350a_minimal": [1.11, 1.76], "rp2350b_minimal": [0.85, 1.41]} mm (DP, DM) where they escape the QFN over the bottom-side fan-out. The reference does not meet its own rule there; at USB full speed and these lengths it is unlikely to matter.

enforced_by: intent impedance (compiled to the DIFF_HS class)

claims.statement: The QSPI pins wire directly to the flash with short connections, for signal integrity and to limit crosstalk.

evidence.note: QFN-80 board: the optional second memory U204 sits on the bottom directly under U202 and its stubs run on B.Cu, so every QSPI net has about 6 mm of track with no ground beside it and 1.3-3.1 mm of top track over cut ground; QFN-60 has none of that (reference/*/measured.json, return_paths).

claims.statement: QSPI_SS has a footprint for a 10 kohm pull-up to 3.3 V (DNF with W25Q128JV) and a 1 kohm series resistor to the BOOTSEL button; both sit close to the flash.
The primary flash is a 25-series QSPI device answering 03h serial read with 24-bit addressing, plus 02h, 05h, 06h and 20h; up to 16 MB (W25Q128JVS on the reference).
A second memory on GPIO0 (XIP_CS1n) needs a 10 kohm pull-up on its chip select, since GPIO0 is pulled low at power-up.
USB_OTP_VDD is always powered at 3.3 V, even when USB is unused; VREG_AVDD is always powered too (it feeds power-on reset and brownout).
I/O connectors carry many ground pins, giving signal return currents short paths.
